Overlap Diagnostics for Group-Time Cells

Source: R/overlap.R
check_overlap.Rd

Covariate-adjusted estimates of \(ATT(g,t)\) need overlap in every group-time cell: each treated unit needs comparison units with similar covariates. check_overlap() reports, for each cell, how much of the treated group lacks that support.

The cells are exactly the ones pte_default() estimates with (same comparison group, base period and anticipation), and the covariates are built the same way as in pte_attgt(): the variables in xformula at the base period, plus changes in the variables in d_covs_formula and, with lagged_outcome_cov = TRUE, the base-period outcome.

Two measures are reported for each cell:

  • Range support: the share of treated units with at least one covariate outside the comparison group's range (its minimum and maximum). For a binary covariate, this is a value no comparison unit has. Being inside the range is necessary, not sufficient, for overlap, but the check works in every cell.

  • Propensity score: the share of treated units whose estimated propensity score (a logit, as in pte_attgt()) is above each of pscore_thresholds. Reported only when the cell has more treated units than covariates (pscore_ok); with fewer, the logit separates whatever the overlap.

With weightsname, every share is also reported weighted by the sampling weights (columns ending in _w). A few heavy treated units outside the comparison range can carry much of a weighted ATT.

This is a diagnostic only; it does not trim or change any estimate.

Usage

check_overlap(
  yname,
  gname,
  tname,
  idname,
  data,
  xformula = ~1,
  d_covs_formula = ~-1,
  lagged_outcome_cov = FALSE,
  weightsname = NULL,
  control_group = "notyettreated",
  base_period = "varying",
  anticipation = 0,
  panel = TRUE,
  pscore_thresholds = c(0.9, 0.999)
)

Arguments

yname

Name of outcome in data

gname

Name of group in data

tname

Name of time period in data

idname

Name of id in data

data

balanced panel or repeated cross sections data

xformula

one-sided formula for covariates used in the propensity score and outcome regression models

d_covs_formula

A formula for time varying covariates to enter the first estimation step models. The default is not to include any, and, hence, to only include pre-treatment covariates.

lagged_outcome_cov

Whether to include the lagged outcome as a covariate. Default is FALSE.

weightsname

The name of the column that contains sampling weights. The default is NULL, in which case no sampling weights are used.

control_group

Which group is used as the comparison group. The default choice is "notyettreated" (units not yet treated in either period of a group-time comparison, including never-treated units). "nevertreated" uses only never-treated units, and "eventuallytreated" uses not-yet-treated units excluding the never treated (as in setup_pte(); units first treated after the last period count as eventually treated). Different estimation strategies can implement their own choices for the control group.

base_period

The type of base period to use. This only affects the numeric value of results in pre-treatment periods. Results in post-treatment periods are not affected by this choice. The default is "varying", where the base period will "back up" to the immediately preceding period in pre-treatment periods. The other option is "universal" where the base period is fixed in pre-treatment periods to be the period right before the treatment starts. "Universal" is commonly used in difference-in-differences applications, but can be unnatural for other identification strategies.

anticipation

how long before the treatment actually takes place it can already affect outcomes, in units of the time variable tname (e.g., years), as in did::att_gt(). With unequally spaced periods this is not the same as a number of periods. Units first treated more than anticipation after the last period are treated as never treated.

panel

Whether the data are panel data. The default is TRUE. Set to FALSE for repeated cross sections.

pscore_thresholds

Propensity score thresholds. The default c(0.9, 0.999) covers the usual trimming rule of thumb (Crump et al., 2009) and the default of did::trimmer().

Value

A data frame of class pte_overlap, one row per group-time cell, with columns

group, time.period

the cell, in units of tname

post

whether the cell is post-treatment

n_treated, n_comparison

numbers of treated and comparison units

n_covariates

number of linearly independent covariates, including the intercept

pscore_ok

whether the propensity score can be estimated (more treated units than covariates)

outside_range

share of treated units outside the comparison range on at least one covariate

worst_covariate

the covariate with the most treated units outside the comparison range (NA if none)

pscore_above_

share of treated units with a propensity score above each threshold (NA if pscore_ok is FALSE)

plus weighted versions of the shares (ending in _w) when weightsname is given. With xformula = ~1 and no other covariates there is nothing to check, and the shares are NA.

References

Crump, R. K., Hotz, V. J., Imbens, G. W. and Mitnik, O. A. (2009). Dealing with limited overlap in estimation of average treatment effects. Biometrika, 96(1), 187-199.

Examples

ov <- check_overlap(
  yname = "lemp", gname = "first.treat", tname = "year",
  idname = "countyreal", data = did::mpdta, xformula = ~lpop
)
ov
#> Overlap diagnostics for 12 group-time cells (7 post-treatment)
#> Post-treatment cells with treated units outside the comparison range: 1 
#> 
#> Worst cells:
#>  group time.period n_treated n_comparison outside_range worst_covariate
#>   2007        2007       131          309       0.00763            lpop
#>  pscore_above_0.9 pscore_above_0.999
#>                 0                  0
